title: MTNR1B rs10830963 Genotype Amplifies Lipid Susceptibility to Poor Circadian Light Hygiene
content: Circadian light exposure influences cardiometabolic health, yet the extent to which genetic variation modifies this relationship remains unclear. We investigated whether MTNR1B rs10830963 genotype modulates blue-light exposure (BLE) patterns and blood lipid profiles in 63 Arctic residents (35 G-carriers) measured around the winter solstice and spring equinox. Participants were stratified by genotype (CC homozygotes vs. G-allele carriers) and contributed weeklong actigraphy data undergoing time-resolved analyses, mixed-effects and cosinor modeling. Genotype-dependent seasonal changes were observed in light-hygiene indices, including the normalized amplitude of BLE (NA BLE) and the nocturnal excess index of BLE (NEI). G-allele carriers also exhibited a less favorable lipid profile, with higher morning LDL-C, TG/HDL-C ratio, and Castelli risk index I, together with lower HDL-C in both seasons. A larger NA BLE was associated with lower TG, TG/HDL-C ratio, and Castelli index, and higher HDL-C, with stronger associations in G-allele carriers. Time-resolved analyses further showed that associations between morning fasting lipid values and 24-h BLE, assessed across 30-min exposure bins within each season, were rhythmically patterned and more pronounced in G-allele carriers, with later acrophases. These findings suggest that MTNR1B rs10830963 modifies the link between seasonal light exposure and lipid metabolism in Arctic residents.
